positive: Many commenters praise the opening and closing animation as smooth, clean and clever, with some saying the design team deserves recognition.
Several say the matte inner screen is a smart way to hide the crease, and some note the crease is barely visible.
Some see the angle-based animations as a sign that apps can detect the hinge position, which could give developers new options.
negative: Many commenters say the crease is still clearly visible, so Apple has not solved it, and some think the matte screen only hides it.
Several worry the crease will get deeper and more noticeable with repeated folding, and that durability and repair costs could be high.
The opening and closing animation draws skepticism: it is seen as a blur that hides viewing-angle issues, and some find the hype overblown.

positive: The opening and closing animations and transitions are widely praised as smooth, fluid and premium-looking.
Some commenters credit Samsung for the screen or say they will stay with Samsung, while a few like specific interface choices such as menu placement.
negative: Many commenters say Samsung and other Android makers released foldables years earlier, so Apple's entry looks late and is not a real innovation.
Others criticise the price, noting that Samsung's foldables are cheaper and often discounted, and that most people cannot afford either.

positive: Several commenters say the Duo's matte inner screen, minimal crease and polished unfolding animation won them over despite initial skepticism.
Some Samsung Fold users prefer the Fold 8's design, citing its thin, light body and squarer shape, while others welcome Apple to foldables.
Some expect Apple's ecosystem, titanium build and interface to give the Duo an edge, and are willing to accept trade-offs like Touch ID.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is years late to foldables and that its fans treat the idea as new, while Samsung and Google got there first.
The Duo's price is seen as too high, with Samsung's Fold described as much cheaper in some countries.
Design gets criticism: the asymmetric, rounded outer shape looks odd when closed, the screen is small, and the phone seems bulky, thick and heavy next to Samsung's slimmer Fold.

positive: Many commenters expected a much higher price and are pleasantly surprised the foldable launched at around the two-thousand-dollar level.
Pricing in line with Samsung's foldable is seen as competitive and normal for this category, even good value when adjusted for inflation.
negative: Many commenters see the foldable's price as excessive and unjustified, saying it works out to roughly the cost of two phones.
Regional pricing draws particular complaints: buyers in India, Turkey, Australia and elsewhere say local prices are much higher and out of reach.
Some say people are too accepting of rising electronics prices, and that a costly foldable isn't worth it when their current phone works fine.

positive: Many commenters prefer a clean, uninterrupted inner display without a cutout or dot, and see the hidden camera as a sensible tradeoff.
Several say they rarely take selfies or photos, or would use the outer-screen camera for selfies, so lower inner camera quality barely matters to them.
Some praise the camera's disappearing effect and the polish of the screen animations, and hope the technology spreads and improves across other phones.
negative: Many say under-display cameras have existed before and were dropped because image quality was poor, so presenting it as a feature seems misleading.
Commenters note the camera is still visible through the screen, so Apple's version is seen as not fully hiding it or doing it well.
Some are frustrated by the high price paired with compromises like weaker camera hardware, missing Face ID, heavy weight and no telephoto lens.

positive: Many left-handed commenters say they have always adapted to right-handed designs, so this phone is not a deal breaker for them.
Several lefties say they already hold their phone in the right hand or use both hands, so the layout barely matters.
Some expect software options to mirror the interface for left-handed users, and a few think the side dock could be more ergonomic for thumbs.
negative: Commenters say the Duo's physical layout, including the fingerprint sensor, outer screen and cameras, favors right-handed use, so software fixes alone wouldn't help left-handed people.
Some left-handed users say they would not buy it or would wait for a later version, rather than hold it awkwardly or upside down.
Others raise wider accessibility and one-handed use worries, such as people with limited use of one arm, and say the larger device is harder to use one-handed.

positive: Some people comparing it with rival foldables see pen support as a clear advantage, and say it could tip their choice toward Apple.
A few note that only the USB-C Pencil appears to work, which means plugging it in to charge or pair.
negative: Many commenters see Apple Pencil support on a foldable as late or unimpressive, saying Apple is copying Samsung rather than innovating.
Some worry a first-generation foldable screen may be fragile or scratch easily with pen use, and that damage would be costly to the owner.
Several people lament that Samsung's foldables lack S Pen support, and criticise the premium price and a rushed-feeling device.

positive: Many commenters praise the smooth open and close transition, especially how content moves seamlessly between the outer and inner screens.
The nano-texture inner display is liked for its matte look, reduced glare and reflections, and for helping hide the fold crease.
Several viewers express excitement or interest in buying the phone, with some favorably comparing it to rival foldables.
negative: Some commenters see "nano-texture" as just a fancy marketing name for a matte screen, not a real innovation.
Several complain the textured display looks grainy once the phone is unfolded, which hurts picture quality.
Others worry about durability and value: an inner screen left open is prone to scratches, and the multitasking benefits seem overstated.

positive: Many commenters are openly excited and plan to preorder or buy as soon as it's available, some setting reminders or trading in current phones.
Long-time owners of older iPhones say this is the upgrade they've waited for, and some are bored with the usual design.
Fans like the look and the different form, and value having one device replace both phone and tablet; camera trade-offs don't bother them.
negative: Price is seen as far too high, so many would stay with a Pro Max or keep their current phone instead.
Many plan to wait for a later generation, expecting first-version flaws, less weight and a more capable Pro-level model.
Concerns about durability and practicality: weight with a case, hinge wear, dust, screen creasing, app scaling, and similarity to an iPad mini.

positive: Several commenters like how the official cases look, saying even a plain design looks clean and appealing once fitted on the phone.
The Apple case reportedly includes a built-in stand, which commenters see as a practical way to prop the foldable up sideways.
Viewers say the case showcase added to their excitement and made some more eager to buy the device.
negative: Cases are seen as adding significant weight, making the already heavy foldable feel bulkier than a small tablet.
Some commenters think a thick case might reduce the device's wobble, though others find the wobble irritating and doubt it fully solves it.
Extra costs like cases and protection plans on top of an already very high price make the phone feel even less worthwhile.
Commenters in Australia and New Zealand find the storage-tier pricing very high, especially for the larger capacities.
Some are disappointed by the color options, wanting black and describing the white as more of an off-white shade.
One viewer notes the inner display's colors look inaccurate, and another cites battery life as a bigger purchase barrier than color or storage.

positive: Many commenters like the compact folded size, saying it fits pockets better and recalling the small iPhone mini while still giving a large unfolded screen.
The new foldable shape is exciting to commenters, who see it as fresh after years of similar designs and say it feels like a meaningful change.
Several praise the software and outer screen, citing smooth transitions between screens, a space-saving side toolbar and easy back-swipe gestures, though some prefer other foldable shapes.
negative: Many commenters say the foldable design is not new, pointing to existing foldables and Microsoft's Surface Duo, and accuse Apple of copying others.
Some worry about durability, saying foldable screens on other brands failed after about a year, which makes them wary of foldables.
Others criticise the high price and missing features such as Face ID, and doubt app support will be ready at launch.

positive: Many commenters praise how smoothly Apple's hardware and software work together, calling the software polished and top quality.
Some say Apple's software and ecosystem are the main reason to choose the device, including for third-party apps and existing Apple users.
Others hope Apple's entry will push developers to optimise apps for foldables, though a few still prefer rival software.
negative: Many commenters say the software features and foldable concept are not new, and that Apple is borrowing ideas from competitors or its own iPadOS.
Some are skeptical about durability and warranty coverage if the screen is opened and closed often.
A few doubt the battery claims will hold up after software updates, and dislike the cover screen's shape when the phone is closed.

positive: Many commenters express strong enthusiasm and eagerness to buy the iPhone Duo, praising its looks, build quality, premium materials and iOS, including some Android users.
Frequent comparisons with Samsung's Fold 8: some say the Duo wins on design, performance and value, while others favour the Fold for lighter weight and features.
Weight is a recurring talking point; the Duo is seen as heavier, which some excuse as a result of premium construction.
negative: Many commenters mock the Duo name and design, saying it looks odd, awkward, or asymmetrical when folded, and that a flip or different name would have suited it better.
Weight and thickness come up often: the phone is described as the heaviest iPhone yet, hard to use one-handed, especially with a case.
Commenters call the price excessive, especially in other countries and for the small base storage, and say it has fewer features than cheaper models.

positive: Some commenters push back on durability worries, noting that the demo unit shown was a plastic dummy while the real phone uses titanium.
Others say the high price is expected for a foldable and reflects the two screens rather than pro-level features.
Many remain excited about the folding animation, iOS ecosystem fit and heavier build, and see little reason to worry about quality.
negative: Many worry the folding crease and hinge will wear out over time, and that the exposed design is easy to damage in a fall.
Commenters say protective cases are hard to find and the device feels fragile, with little protection for the screen.
The device is seen as heavy and bulky, and the very high price makes the durability risk feel less acceptable.

positive: Viewers praise the design and software, especially the opening animation and how well the interface suits the device, and they like the look in reviews.
Many see practical value in the larger screen for reading documents, medical charts, school work or waiting time, and some plan to buy it despite the price.
Commenters compare it with other foldables from Samsung, Google and OnePlus; some stay loyal to Android, others are tied to Apple's ecosystem.
negative: Many commenters praise the video but say they won't buy the Duo, mainly because it is a pricey first-generation product.
Camera compromises and missing features, such as Face ID and Pro-level effects, are seen as poor value compared with regular Pro phones.
Some raise design worries, including hinge durability after drops and rounded corners that reduce usable screen space, and some prefer other foldables.

positive: Many commenters see the foldable as a way to replace or carry less of an iPad, combining phone and tablet in one device.
The larger inner screen is praised for media, reading, viewing plans or photos, and larger text, with the matte finish also welcomed.
Some like the polished software touches, such as screen transitions and button placement, and expect the developer push to improve tablet app versions.
negative: Many see the foldable as essentially a small tablet at a very high price, with a modest screen-size gain and little that feels new.
Commenters dislike the matte inner screen, calling it dull and hard to see in sunlight, and note the visible crease and screen fragility.
Software and hardware gaps draw criticism: limited split-screen layouts, few dock apps, fiddly multitasking gestures, and no stylus support despite the large display.

positive: Many commenters like that iOS was redesigned for the foldable, with better multitasking and thoughtful layout choices such as a movable dock and unchanged app widths.
Some prefer iOS for its simplicity and say Apple's entry is what finally makes them want a foldable, even over stronger Android options, or tempts them to switch back.
Reactions are eager overall: people plan to buy, find the design appealing, and think the price is more tolerable than expected, with some praising the fingerprint sensor.
negative: Commenters say Android foldables have offered the same features since 2019, so Apple's version feels late and gives Android users little reason to switch.
Many complain about the price, especially outside the US, where local costs look far higher than the US sticker price, plus tax.
Some criticise Apple's iOS multitasking and camera quality, and doubt the design and presentation, including the crease illusion and the unfolding animation.

positive: Commenters praise the engineering and design, saying the team deserves credit and that the device feels distinct rather than a copy of other foldables.
The one-sided rounded edge draws approval: it recalls a small notebook, feels soft in a pocket, and looks good when opened.
Several viewers like the glass-style opening animation and say the Liquid Glass interface suits the foldable well.
negative: Commenters see the hinge as unremarkable or derivative, similar to existing foldables from rivals, and find the reviewer's amazement unwarranted.
Some doubt that a water-resistance rating means real durability, pointing to a rival foldable that had the rating yet still failed.
Viewers feel the design cuts corners and the price is too high for the storage offered.

positive: Many commenters are excited for the foldable and plan to wait and buy it at launch, including long-time Apple fans.
Some are holding off on buying to compare other phones, especially for camera quality, even though they like the design.
Viewers like practical features such as a usable viewfinder with the main cameras, a bedside stand mode, and a fun front display for photos.
negative: Many commenters say foldable phones are not new and feel Apple is arriving late, while reviewers treat it as a breakthrough.
Some suspect Apple left out flagship features like the telephoto camera on purpose, saving them for a later model and making early adopters compromise.
Others criticise the high price, the closed shape and display compromises, and expect more from a company of Apple's size.
Many commenters say the Duo's cameras are a downgrade from the Pro models and don't justify its price. Some want the Pro's main lens or telephoto.
Price is a major complaint, with commenters in several countries calling the base model far too expensive, especially once local taxes are included.
Other gripes include a matte display, missing face unlock, weaker battery, extra weight and no mute button compared with the Pro Max.

positive: Some commenters welcome the return of fingerprint unlocking, finding it faster and more practical than face scanning, especially when sitting at a desk.
Others argue Face ID is the better system and see fingerprint sensors as inferior.
Watch-based unlocking was mentioned as a feature that removes the lack of face recognition as a dealbreaker for some.
negative: Some would rather have Touch ID back for security, though they admit Face ID is more convenient.
Others worry about the device's thickness and weight, and about fingerprints smudging the surface.

positive: Many commenters repeat a pun on Apple leadership, saying earlier executives laid the groundwork and a new leader now takes over.
Several joke that the foldable's wider screen lets them watch a recent Nolan film in the format the director intended.
Others praise the fold animation and the see-through look of the front panel, and some say they plan to buy one.
